solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: F1 driver leaving hotel in Bow, or somewhere else in London? (8)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the hotel's letters go out of the driver's name
indicatorNotes.in Bow: Bow is in the East End, where cockneys drop their Hs, so HILTON is said 'ILTON

blocks.clueFragment: F1 driver leaving hotel in Bow
blocks.note: LEWIS HAMILTON without ILTON, the Hilton hotel as a cockney would say it

annotation.surface: A racing driver checks out of his East London hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of London's East End, home of the cockney who drops the H; so the hotel is 'ILTON, not HILTON. Lewisham is a borough of south-east London, hence 'somewhere else'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lewisham is a London borough, a different place in London from Bow.

entries.clue: Magazine of old on chic way of conducting oneself (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, LIFE sits on top of STYLE

blocks.note: Life, the American photo magazine that stopped weekly publication in 1972

annotation.surface: An old glossy magazine offers tips on elegant behaviour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an etiquette column; 'magazine' is a specific title, LIFE.
annotation.definitionFit: A lifestyle is the way a person lives and conducts themselves.

entries.clue: State of the Union? (7)

blocks.note: the surface wants a nation or a speech; here it means a condition someone lives in
not the United States but the union of two people at a wedding; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: The US President's annual address to Congress.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is the American presidential speech; read 'union' as the union of two people and 'state' as condition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: the marital union is a condition, and the old legal word for being in it is the answer.

entries.clue: Force as yet skipping shelter (6)

indicatorNotes.skipping: the letters jump about into a new order

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force

annotation.surface: Someone is pressed to leave cover before they are ready.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skipping' looks like leaving something out, but nothing is omitted: F joins AS YET and the six letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Safety is a place of protection, a shelter from harm.

entries.clue: Presenter’s article on new Republican carrying little weight (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, AN comes above the rest
indicatorNotes.carrying: N and R carry OUNCE between them

blocks.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight, about 28 grams

annotation.surface: A broadcaster's piece about a fresh Republican candidate who carries little clout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Presenter’s' reads as possessive, but the ’s is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An announcer presents programmes or news on radio or television.

entries.clue: Hard worker from city of Paris (6)

blocks.note: from the idiom for toiling tirelessly, named after the defenders of a besieged city
Paris, prince of Troy, whose city was Troy

annotation.surface: A diligent labourer who comes from the French capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Paris is not the French capital but the Trojan prince who carried off Helen; his city is Troy.
annotation.definitionFit: A Trojan is proverbially a tireless worker, as in 'work like a Trojan'.

entries.clue: Barber swayed and walked unsteadily (7)

blocks.note: Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street

annotation.surface: A drunken barber lurches and staggers home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swayed' looks like part of the staggering, but it means influenced, LED.
annotation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short unsteady steps, like a small child.

entries.clue: Order European to support island party in show of respect (9)

indicatorNotes.to support: in a down clue, E goes underneath IS and ANC, holding them up

blocks.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire
the ANC, South Africa's African National Congress party

annotation.surface: A command for a European to back an island's political party as a mark of deference.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command; it is the honour, the OBE.
annotation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of deference, such as a bow: a show of respect.

entries.clue: Courts going round American state (7)

indicatorNotes.going round: to go round something is to encircle it, so the courts wrap themselves around the American

blocks.note: an atrium is an open central court, plural atria

annotation.surface: Law courts are travelling round an American state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American state' looks like one phrase; American gives US, and 'state' alone is the definition, a country.
annotation.definitionFit: Austria is a sovereign state in central Europe.

entries.clue: Agent regularly offends (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

annotation.surface: An agent who keeps getting into trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: A fed is American slang for an FBI agent.
annotation.definitionFit: A fed is a federal agent, especially of the FBI.

entries.clue: Frances’s empty day unravelling costume (5,5)

indicatorNotes.empty: DAY with its inside gone leaves D and Y
indicatorNotes.unravelling: the letters come undone and are rewoven

blocks.note: the name with the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: Frances has a day with nothing to do while her outfit comes apart.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S is part of the fodder, so all ten letters are FRANCESS plus DY.
annotation.definitionFit: Fancy dress is costume worn to dress up as someone or something else.

entries.clue: What saves time is suggestion of copper? (5,3)

blocks.note: a short haircut suggests a copper, a policeman, famously short-back-and-sides

annotation.surface: A time-saving tip hints at copper.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer; the question mark flags that a short cut of hair only suggests one.
annotation.definitionFit: A short cut is a quicker way of doing something, so it saves time.

entries.clue: Distinction one craves, reportedly (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: the answer sounds like what is described

blocks.note: one who craves, or lusts, is a luster

annotation.surface: Someone longs for renown.
annotation.walkthrough: LUSTRE is the British spelling; it sounds the same as LUSTER, one who lusts.
annotation.definitionFit: Lustre is glory or distinction, as in adding lustre to a reputation.

entries.clue: Bondage of peasant never-ending (4)

indicatorNotes.never-ending: the word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A peasant's servitude goes on for ever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Never-ending' reads as eternal bondage; it only trims the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: the wooden frame on draught oxen stands for subjection, as in 'the yoke of tyranny'.

entries.clue: Cook a nice dahl and another dish (9)

indicatorNotes.Cook: the letters are cooked into something new

annotation.surface: An instruction to make a good dahl and a second dish besides.
annotation.walkthrough: Dahl is itself a dish, so the definition says 'another'.
annotation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a tortilla rolled round a filling.

entries.clue: Chance western must be given new beginning (10)

indicatorNotes.given new beginning: the first letter is replaced by a different one

blocks.note: O swapped for A at the front

annotation.surface: A cowboy film needs a fresh opening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests a cowboy film; it is the adjective OCCIDENTAL. The new first letter is unclued, so crossings pin it.
annotation.definitionFit: Chance, as an adjective, means happening by accident: accidental.

entries.clue: At sea mostly (2,3,4)

blocks.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a set phrase meaning for the most part, generally

annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' also means confused, which is the tempting reading; here it is literal, out on the main.
annotation.definitionFit: In the main means generally or mostly, and literally on the open sea.

entries.clue: Doctor slanders university washerwoman (9)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

annotation.surface: A physician badmouths a college laundry worker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person doing the slandering; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman who washes clothes for a living.

entries.clue: Those returning members choose to speak (10)

blocks.note: to orate is to speak formally

annotation.surface: Returning club members pick someone to address them.
annotation.walkthrough: To return a member is to elect an MP to Parliament; those who do it are the voters.
annotation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters who return members to Parliament.

entries.clue: I am troubled about offspring’s affair (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'about turn': facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: I AIL (I am troubled) turned round

annotation.surface: A parent is worried about a child's romance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning'; it turns I AIL round. The ’s is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the romantic sense: an illicit relationship, borrowed from the French word for a link.

entries.clue: Dispensing with hat, initially get too hot in gorge (7)

indicatorNotes.Dispensing with: to dispense with something is to do without it, so that letter is left out
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of 'hat' is meant

blocks.note: to overheat is to get too hot

annotation.surface: Taking off your hat to stop overheating in a ravine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' reads as a ravine; it is the verb, to stuff oneself. OVERHEAT without H gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat too much: to overeat.

entries.clue: Teresa uncertainly restraining hairy man (4)

indicatorNotes.restraining: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: four letters straddle the join, starting at the second letter of Teresa

annotation.surface: Teresa hesitantly holds back a hirsute man.
annotation.walkthrough: In Genesis Esau is 'an hairy man', the twin of smooth-skinned Jacob.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by biblical description: Genesis calls Jacob's twin 'an hairy man', set against smooth Jacob.

entries.clue: Heartache of daughter when getting up before noon on English boat (7)

indicatorNotes.getting up: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so D AS is reversed
indicatorNotes.before: 'before' means earlier in order, so the reversed piece is placed ahead of the noon letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the pieces above sit on SS

annotation.surface: A daughter wakes before midday on an English boat, heartbroken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When' gives AS, as in 'as I left'. 'Getting up' reads as rising from bed; in a down clue it reverses.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: heartache is emotional pain rather than a physical ache of the heart.

entries.clue: Nightmare examination holding back Miliband? (6)

indicatorNotes.holding: ORAL holds the other piece inside
indicatorNotes.back: to go back is to go the opposite way, so the name is read from its end

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam
Ed Miliband, former leader of the UK Labour Party, gives ED, turned back

annotation.surface: An exam that holds back a politician is a bad dream.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Miliband is only an example of an Ed; either David or Ed Miliband fits the surface, but only Ed gives letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, harrowing experience, a nightmare.

entries.clue: Sex twists in court case (6)

indicatorNotes.twists: a twist turns something round, so the numeral faces the other way
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means placed inside, so the twisted numeral sits within the courting word

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
to court someone is to date them

annotation.surface: A sex scandal takes a turn in a court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court case' paints a trial, but 'court' is the verb DATE and 'case' alone is grammatical. Sex is Latin for six.
annotation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking the indirect object.

entries.clue: Humiliated and given low mark, I hear (8)

indicatorNotes.I hear: what follows is said out loud

blocks.note: given a D, a poor grade

annotation.surface: A student is humiliated by a poor grade.
annotation.walkthrough: D is a low grade in school marking, so being D-graded is getting a low mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean brought low in dignity, the past participle matching 'Humiliated'.

entries.clue: Losing head, run off with Polish rascal (10)

indicatorNotes.Losing head: the word drops its first letter
indicatorNotes.with: one piece is set alongside the other

annotation.surface: A decapitated man escapes with a Pole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is polish, refinement.
annotation.definitionFit: A scapegrace is a mischievous or unprincipled person, a rascal.

entries.clue: First mate never taking jacket off (3)

indicatorNotes.taking jacket off: the outer letters, the word's jacket, are removed

annotation.surface: A ship's first mate who never removes a coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First mate' reads as a ship's officer; it is the first wife, Adam's mate.
annotation.definitionFit: In Genesis Eve was Adam's mate, the first woman.

entries.clue: Little one really making Charlie nervous at first (6)

indicatorNotes.making: 'making X Y' means turning X into Y, so Charlie's letter becomes the other
indicatorNotes.at first: only the first letter of nervous is used

blocks.note: C (Charlie in the phonetic alphabet) becomes N, first letter of nervous

annotation.surface: A small child genuinely scares Charlie.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet; swap it for N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'little one' is an affectionate phrase for a baby or small child.

entries.clue: Sly Asian sabotaged investigation (8)

indicatorNotes.sabotaged: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A cunning saboteur derails an inquiry.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder sits in plain sight at the front of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are close examinations of something to find out how it works.
